```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab04", title = "Nonseasonal ARIMA")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "ARIMA(1,1,0): c=0.2, phi=0.5, y_4=14, difference at t=4 is 3. One-step level forecast yhat_5 is:",
  q2 = "When d=1, a nonzero constant c is:",
  q3 = "SES / ETS(A,N,N) is the ARIMA cousin of:",
  q4 = "In one or two sentences, what would you tell a policy analyst about Spain GDP forecasts (scale and baseline)?"
)
```

## What you will do

Finish the ARIMA(1,1,0) hand forecast and interpret drift vs mean.

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `fpp3`, `learnr`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.


```{r hand, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
c0 <- 0.2
phi <- 0.5
dy4 <- 3
y4 <- 14
dyhat <- c0 + phi * dy4
y4 + dyhat
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("15.7", correct = TRUE),
  answer("1.7"),
  answer("14.2"),
  answer("17"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("A drift (average change per period)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The mean of the levels"),
  answer("A seasonal intercept"),
  answer("The MA coefficient"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("(0,1,1)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("(0,1,0)"),
  answer("(1,0,0)"),
  answer("(0,2,2)"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Log then difference; compare to RW-with-drift; accuracy on the GDP scale.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Answer the questions above first, type your name, download the `.txt`, and upload it.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
